judged_text: Blacklist filtering compares raw-case guest emails against a lowercased blacklist, so 'Spam@X.com' bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS while 'spam@x.com' is filtered. blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased but the incoming guest string is not, so a mixed-case variant of a blacklisted address skips the filter: the guest is added to the booking and emailed, and because the dedup check (guest === attendee.email, also case-sensitive) stores the cased variant, the same address can be added again as 'other case' — the blacklist is silently bypassable and duplicate-variant emails accumulate.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but the filter checks `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, so mixed-case variants of a blacklisted email can bypass the blacklist. Similarly, deduping against existing attendees uses a case-sensitive equality (`guest === attendee.email`), and the server schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` does not enforce uniqueness/case normalization, allowing the same email to be added multiple times with different casing.
